reviewed_behavior.assessment: Only valid run IDs and the prepared/observed/closed hashed-run filenames reach retained PrivateJournal directory FD. At most three reports, each containing fixed kind, raw byte length and 64-character lowercase raw SHA-256. No journal bytes, path, argv, environment or parsed evidence returned. No trust, recovery or authority constructor added.

Original directory capability uses descriptor-relative no-follow traversal. Each inspected artifact has no-follow pre-entry regular-file/effective-UID/single-link/private-mode/512KiB checks; nonblocking no-follow open; matching descriptor device/inode plus private ownership/type/size; bounded read with one-byte sentinel; post-read descriptor metadata equality including timestamps; post-entry type/device/inode/UID/link/mode/size; directory validation before/after. Returned errors are static labels. No pathname reopening redirects the file read.

Boxed fixed [Option<HistoricalResourceSample>;8] stores oldest-first last eight runtime-recorded Observed snapshots having at least one dynamic known scalar/counter/flag. Static pids.max and memory.max never qualify. Samples retain full metric unknown reasons, owner digest/device/inode and original attempt number; no count is synthesized from limits. Eviction and insertion are fixed bounded work.

Before a6df, Observed event containers whose known members were all None incorrectly counted as useful and could evict genuine history. Final code requires at least one Some member for pids/memory/cgroup event containers. is_some counts zero and false correctly; test adds the all-None counterexample. Known scalar Observed fields remain qualifying.

before/latest/final/failure semantics unchanged: Observed all-unknown snapshot may still become latest; history retention does not reinterpret it. sample_attempts increments on every non-frozen sample. Final closure installs existing private frozen fence before cloning; record returns without changes when frozen. History is excluded from authoritative closure tuple via unchanged authoritative_binding/closure digest. Private fence remains skipped on serde; JSON cannot reconstruct closure capability.

Struct-level legacy defaults populate absent history with eight None entries; native serde array length requires exactly eight when present. Fixed count and numeric metric shape bound runtime-produced growth; sampled owner digest is generated internally. Per-artifact reader/writer cap remains512KiB. No backend/admission limit was reduced or bypassed.

test_source_assessment.adequacy: Meaningful behavior and hostile-file coverage for this bounded advisory change. Existing frozen/closure tests serialize the expanded diagnostics and therefore cover new history too. Reviewer inspected test source only and claims no test execution or count.
nonblocking_coverage_limits: Positive Some(0)/Some(false) fixture also has known dynamic scalar readings, so event-only zero/false qualification is not isolated as a test. Final explicit is_some source is correct.
Wrong array test uses too-short length; fixed-size serde array also rejects overlength by construction, but no new explicit length9 case was added.
No deterministic concurrent overwrite/rename-at-read hook is exercised by the new tests; metadata guards were assessed statically.

limits: The three artifact hashes are sequential sampled metadata, not one atomic journal snapshot, lifecycle completeness proof, evidence validation or recovery authorization. Missing/open-raced-away entries can be absent from a report.

Pre/post checks detect ordinary concurrent changes; they cannot make a security boundary against root or arbitrary same-UID mutation after the last check. Metadata can become stale immediately after sampling.
Reads are byte-bounded regular-file I/O, not a hard wall-clock guarantee for every filesystem/storage failure.

The8-slot bound covers runtime-produced diagnostic collections; public diagnostic Deserialize still requires caller transport/JSON bounds and does not authenticate owner_digest or samples. Existing public fields/serde trust semantics are unchanged.
sample_attempts and stored attempt numbers saturate at u32MAX as before; sequence numbers then cease to be strictly increasing. They are advisory, not timestamps or unique authority IDs.

More history can increase advisory closed-journal bytes; unchanged512KiB cap still fails closed. No resource-exhaustion cause, live Linux qualification, provider behavior, admission/current-authority policy, dispatch or recovery claim follows.
No new auth boundary or external route was added; inspect_run_journal is a trusted in-process executor metadata seam.
